name: wiz3D — DX7/DX8/DX9/DX10/DX11 Wrappers
description: Lightweight stereo-3D injection wrappers (effcol). Wraps DirectX 7 / 8 / 9 / 10-11 / 12 and Vulkan to add stereoscopic 3D to games that don't natively render it. Originally targeted iZ3D-supported titles, now works with most games. The DX9-DX11 wrappers also hook into games that shipped with DirectX Automatic Mode support (in-game 3D toggles, separation/convergence sliders), driving those controls from the wrapper. Stereopticon downloads wiz3D from its upstream GitHub release at setup time rather than bundling — wiz3D's LGPL-2.1 isn't directly compatible with GPL-3.0 distribution, and this also keeps users on the latest build. Config via wiz3D_Config.xml dropped next to the game exe.
license: LGPL-2.1 (not bundled — fetched at setup from upstream releases)

latest.wiz3d_advanced_outputs_notes: These map to historical 3D hardware (vintage HMDs like eMagin Z800, Vuzix VR920; passive 3D monitors like Zalman, Taerim, Avitrid; DLP/CRT shutter variants; iZ3D's own dual-projection mode). Fixes targeting this hardware should select the specific class via tool_config rather than the high-level native_outputs field.
latest.notes: General-purpose stereo injection. For games rendering 3D themselves (3D Vision Direct Mode, AMD HD3D, OpenGL quad-buffer), use the dedicated wiz3d_* tool variants instead.
